newsitem.title: USA: Missouri's crop conditions sag on hot weather.
newsitem.headline: Missouri's crop conditions sag on hot weather.

text.p: Missouri's crop conditions declined last week because of hot weather, according to the Missouri Agricultural Statistics Service.

Corn conditions were one percent very poor, eight percent poor, 36 percent fair, 44 percent good and 11 percent excellent, a moderate decline from last wek's favorable rating. Fifty-nine percent of the crop was silking or beyond and fourteen percent of the crop has reached the dough stage.
Soybeans were six percent excellent, 44 percent good, 37 percent fair, 11 percent poor and two percent very poor.
Forty percent of soybeans were blooming.
The wheat harvest was virtually complete and topsoil moisture levels were 10 percent very short, 50 percent short, 38 percent adequate and two percent surplus.
Pasture and range conditions were two percent excellent, 34 percent good, 40 percent fair, 21 percent poor and three percent very poor.
Ninety percent of the cotton crop was squaring. Cotton conditions were four percent excellent, 48 percent good, 38 percent fair, five percent poor and five percent very poor.
